name: Instagram
tagline: Photo and video sharing app with a feed, stories, reels and DMs, owned by Meta.

pricing.plan: Free, with a paid Meta Verified tier
pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified. Core app is free and ad-supported; Meta Verified is the paid add-on.

verdictSummary: The software here is not the hard part: an agent can build you an image feed with captions, likes and comments in an afternoon. What you cannot build is the two billion people already posting there, plus everyone you know checking it out of habit. Instagram is a distribution channel first and a photo app a distant second, so a private clone gives you a photo journal with an empty follower count. There is also the boring heavy stuff: video transcoding, CDN delivery, moderation, and a recommendation system trained on years of engagement data. Build the personal archive if you want your pictures off Meta's servers, but do not pretend it replaces the app.
coreLoopDIY: A single-user, self-hosted photo and video journal: upload media, add captions and tags, browse a chronological grid and feed, and export everything as files plus JSON.
requirements: a machine or VPS to host it
ffmpeg installed for video thumbnails and transcodes
an Instagram data export if you want to import your history
whatYouLose: The audience: nobody follows your self-hosted feed, so posting into it is journaling, not publishing
Discovery and the recommendation engine, which is most of what people actually open the app for
DMs, which for many users are the real product
The mobile capture experience: camera, stickers, one-tap stories, editing tools that feel instant
Reels-grade video pipeline, CDN delivery and playback that never buffers
moatNotes: Two-sided in a subtle way: creators go where the viewers are, viewers go where the creators are, and the ranking model that keeps both is fed by engagement data nobody else has.
whyPeopleStillPay: Almost nobody pays Instagram cash, they pay in attention and ads, and that trade only works because everyone else made it too. People stay because their friends, their customers, their photographer, their old classmates and their favorite accounts are all in one app with a shared set of norms. Even users who dislike it keep the account open as a searchable social address. The paid tier, Meta Verified, sells a badge and support access, which is really just a tax on caring about that reach.
notes: You can clone the interface in a weekend and it will feel like a very nice empty room. The moat is the network: every person you know already checking the same app, and the ranking data that keeps them scrolling.
prompt:
Build a self-hosted, single-user photo and video journal. Think "my Instagram archive, minus Instagram".

Stack, no substitutions:
- Next.js 14 App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, file at ./data/app.db
- Media stored on local disk at ./data/media, originals untouched
- sharp for image thumbnails, ffmpeg (assume it is on PATH) for video posters and a 720p web copy
- Single password login from ADMIN_PASSWORD in .env, signed httpOnly cookie session. No user accounts, no OAuth, no third-party services, no analytics.

In scope:
- Upload page: drag and drop multiple images and videos, show progress, dedupe by SHA-256 of the file
- On upload, read EXIF for capture date, camera and GPS, store it, then write a stripped copy for anything served publicly
- Post model: one or more media items, caption with markdown, tags, taken_at, created_at, optional place string, optional private flag
- Chronological feed view and a square grid view, both infinite scroll, newest first
- Post detail page with full-size viewer, arrow key navigation, and EXIF panel
- Filter by tag, by year and month, and full-text search over captions using SQLite FTS5
- Import command: `npm run import -- path/to/instagram-export` that walks a Meta data export, parses the JSON, and creates posts with original timestamps
- Export command that writes every original file plus a posts.json manifest to a folder
- Nightly cron-friendly script that verifies every DB row still has its file on disk and prints orphans

Out of scope, do not build: followers, likes, comments, DMs, stories, notifications, an algorithmic feed, filters and photo editing, any public multi-user mode.

Deliverables: working app on `npm run dev`, a seed script that generates 40 fake posts with placeholder images, a README with setup and the import/export commands, and .env.example listing ADMIN_PASSWORD only.
